question: Solid CO₂ gets converted directly into gaseous state on decrease of pressure to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 atmosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Solid CO2, commonly known as dry ice, sublimates directly into the gaseous state at atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere).
 
• Sublimation of CO2 occurs at a temperature of -78.5°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure.
 
• At pressures lower than 5.1 atmospheres, CO2 cannot exist in the liquid state and directly converts between solid and gas phases.
 
• This property of CO2 is utilized in various applications such as refrigeration, where dry ice is used to keep items cold without leaving any residue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation**

 
 
• Sublimation is the process by which a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• This endothermic phase transition occurs under specific temperature and pressure conditions.
 
 
 
• **Triple Point of CO2**
 
 
• The triple point of CO2 is the condition of temperature and pressure at which CO2 can coexist in solid, liquid, and gaseous states.
 
• For CO2, the triple point is at 5.1 atmospheres and -56.6°C.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Dry Ice**
 
 
• Dry ice is used for refrigeration, especially for shipping perishable goods, as it sublimates without leaving a liquid residue.
 
• It is also used in theatrical productions to create fog effects and in scientific experiments requiring low temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• Handling dry ice requires gloves and protective clothing to prevent frostbite, as it is extremely cold.
 
• Proper ventilation is necessary when using dry ice to avoid the buildup of CO2 gas, which can be hazardous in enclosed spaces.
